newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bonos/bund spread to stall at 150 bps - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Bonos/bund spread to stall at 150 bps - analysts.

text.p: Spain's 10-year cash spread over Bunds should find a top at around 150 basis points, analysts said on Monday.
"I think 150 basis points could be an important psychological level," said Valentin Fernandez, economist at Credit Lyonnais.
The spread was trading at 140 basis points on Monday versus 130 on Friday, after the Bank of Spain shaved 25 basis points off its key money market rate to 5.75 percent in its second cut of the year.

Peripheral markets came under pressure on Monday after negative EMU comments by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel. Waigel told a German newspaper that EMU criteria were more important than a timetable.
The onslaught of a series of EMU jitters has led to a widening of the 10-year cash spread over Bunds since January when excitement over the two countries joining a single currency reached its height.
"If meeting the Maastricht criteria is what matters, and Germany is not, we could see a delay in the whole project," said Carmen Hernansanz, economist of Merrill Lynch in Madrid.
Analysts added that Europe's southern markets, or the so-called "Club-med", would suffer most from a delay, having benefited most from optimism over Euro convergence.
Difficulties in approving the Italian mini-budget were adding pressure to Spain's bonos.
Analysts said bonds had been finding it difficult to react positively to good news, and were overreacting to bad news, in recent days.
Spain's bonos, for example, shrugged off comments from central bank governor Luis Angel Rojo over the week end that the inflation trend was improving.
"Overall I am optimistic enough about the inflation and economic trend", Rojo said on Sunday.

Also positive and unexpected news about February inflation, which fell to 2.5 percent year-on-year from 2.9 percent in January, and the central bank cut were largely ignored by the long end of the bond market.

"The situation is rather different compared with the last rate cut in January. Peseta weakness and Euro jitters regarding the possibility of EMU delay causes the difference" Bank of America said in a research note on Monday.
Spanish economists said they were optimistic for more rate cuts this year.
"We still think that the key money market rate could end the year at around 5.0-5.25 pct", Societe Generale said in a note to clients.
